passage:
New students often got lost during the first week of school. The buildings looked similar, and the signs were small.
The student council decided to make a new map. Instead of only drawing buildings, they added helpful details: the quietest staircase, the water machine that worked best, the sunny place to eat lunch, and the classroom that was easy to miss.
Teachers checked the map for accuracy, and students drew small pictures to make it friendly.
When the new school year began, the map was given to every new student. Many said it helped them feel less nervous.
A good map does not only show where places are. It also shows that someone has thought about the person using it.
